    Egger's regression test for funnel plot asymmetry

    Source: R/meta-bias.R
    meta_egger.Rd

    meta_egger() regresses effect sizes on their standard errors (or sampling variances) to test for small-study effects. With model = "lm" this is the classical weighted least squares test of Egger et al. (1997), with a multiplicative dispersion term. With model = "rma" the predictor is added to a mixed-effects meta-regression with additive heterogeneity (Sterne and Egger, 2005). The intercept is the limit estimate, the expected effect in a study with infinite precision.

    Usage

    meta_egger(
  .data,
  yi = .yi,
  vi = .vi,
  predictor = c("sei", "vi"),
  model = c("lm", "rma"),
  method = "REML",
  level = 0.95
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame, <meta_es> or <meta_fit> from meta_pool().

    yi, vi

    <data-masking> Columns holding the effect sizes and sampling variances. Default to .yi and .vi.

    predictor

    "sei" (standard error, Egger's test) or "vi" (sampling variance).

    model

    "lm" or "rma".

    method

    Estimator of \(\tau^2\) for model = "rma". Taken from the fit when .data is a <meta_fit>.

    level

    Confidence level for intervals.

    Value

    A one row tibble with the slope test (estimate, std.error, statistic, df, p.value) and the limit estimate with its confidence interval.

    References

    Egger, M., Davey Smith, G., Schneider, M. and Minder, C. (1997). Bias in meta-analysis detected by a simple, graphical test. BMJ, 315(7109), 629-634. doi:10.1136/bmj.315.7109.629

    Sterne, J. A. C. and Egger, M. (2005). Regression methods to detect publication and other bias in meta-analysis. In H. R. Rothstein, A. J. Sutton and M. Borenstein (Eds.), Publication Bias in Meta-Analysis (pp. 99-110). Wiley.

    Examples

    bcg <- meta_effect_size(bcg_trials, "RR",
  event1 = tpos, n1 = tpos + tneg, event2 = cpos, n2 = cpos + cneg
)
meta_egger(bcg)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 11
#>   test  predictor model estimate std.error statistic    df p.value
#>   <chr> <chr>     <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl> <int>   <dbl>
#> 1 Egger sei       lm       -2.11      1.51     -1.40    11   0.189
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: limit_estimate <dbl>, limit_conf.low <dbl>,
#> #   limit_conf.high <dbl>
meta_pool(bcg) |> meta_egger(model = "rma")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 11
#>   test  predictor model estimate std.error statistic    df p.value
#>   <chr> <chr>     <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl> <int>   <dbl>
#> 1 Egger sei       rma     -0.763     0.950    -0.803    NA   0.422
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: limit_estimate <dbl>, limit_conf.low <dbl>,
#> #   limit_conf.high <dbl>
